text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today after dropping sharply over the past two weeks, likely bouncing back on relief that potential U.S.-Iran negotiations could ease global oil supply tensions. The stock has been volatile since late October amid leadership changes at the company and uncertainty over fuel supplies — gasoline and diesel inventories remain tight relative to refining capacity (92.8% utilization), which has been propping up margins for refiners even as crude oil prices have surged to $103 domestically and $123 globally.

The broader picture is one of conflicting signals for the refining sector. While high oil and fuel prices have boosted refining profit margins significantly, investors are cautious ahead of earnings announcements because guidance about future production and demand will determine whether these elevated margins stick around. The stock's 7% decline over two weeks reflects uncertainty about whether current conditions are sustainable or whether supply pressures will ease.
